scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oils- Oil Palm
description:
The National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm was launched in August 2021 by the Government of India. 

This initiative aims to reduce the country's dependence on edible oil imports. 

India is one of the largest consumers of edible oils in the world. 

In 2020-2021, India imported around 14 million metric tons of edible oils. 

The expenditure on these imports was approximately INR 1.17 lakh crore. 

The mission seeks to enhance domestic production of edible oils, particularly palm oil. 

The government has set a target to achieve self-sufficiency in edible oil production by 2025-2026. 

The specific goal is to increase the area under oil palm cultivation to 6.5 lakh hectares by 2025-2026. 

This is expected to produce around 11 lakh metric tons of crude palm oil annually. 

The mission is part of the broader Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. 

It aims to make India self-reliant in various sectors, including agriculture. 

The National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The mission focuses on promoting oil palm cultivation in suitable agro-climatic zones. 

These zones include the northeastern states and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. 

The government has identified around 1.5 million hectares of land for potential oil palm cultivation. 

The mission provides financial assistance to farmers for establishing oil palm plantations. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 29,000 per hectare for the first five years. 

This assistance covers the cost of planting material, fertilizers, and other inputs. 

The government also supports the establishment of processing units for palm oil. 

Processing units will be set up to ensure value addition and better price realization for farmers. 

The government aims to establish at least 20 processing units across the country. 

These units will help in processing crude palm oil into refined oil. 

The mission also emphasizes research and development in oil palm cultivation. 

The Indian Council of Agricultural Research is involved in developing high-yielding varieties. 

The government encourages public-private partnerships to enhance investment in the sector. 

The mission aims to create a sustainable oil palm industry in India. 

It is expected to generate employment opportunities in rural areas. 

The mission has the potential to create around 1.5 lakh jobs directly and indirectly. 

The government has also launched awareness programs for farmers. 

These programs aim to educate farmers about oil palm cultivation techniques. 

The mission includes training sessions and workshops for farmers. 

The government has set up a dedicated helpline for farmers seeking assistance. 

Farmers can contact the helpline for guidance on oil palm cultivation. 

The mission also aims to promote the use of technology in oil palm farming. 

Digital platforms will be utilized for monitoring and support. 

The government plans to provide subsidies for drip irrigation systems. 

This will help in efficient water management for oil palm cultivation. 

The National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm is expected to contribute to food security. 

It will also play a significant role in enhancing farmers' incomes. 

The mission aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

The government aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices through this mission. 

The mission is expected to have a positive impact on the environment. 

Oil palm cultivation requires less land compared to other oilseed crops. 

This can help in reducing deforestation and preserving biodiversity. 

The government has allocated INR 11,040 crore for the mission over a period of five years. 

This funding will support various initiatives under the mission. 

The mission also aims to improve the livelihoods of small and marginal farmers. 

The government encourages the participation of women in oil palm cultivation. 

Women farmers will receive special training and support under the mission. 

The mission will also promote cooperative farming models. 

Cooperatives can help farmers in collective marketing and processing. 

The government aims to enhance the competitiveness of the oil palm sector. 

This will be achieved through better infrastructure and market access. 

The mission will also focus on developing supply chains for palm oil. 

The government plans to establish linkages between farmers and processors. 

This will ensure fair prices for farmers and reduce market volatility. 

The mission is expected to have a multiplier effect on the rural economy. 

It will contribute to the overall growth of the agricultural sector. 

The government will regularly monitor the progress of the mission. 

Performance indicators will be established to assess the impact. 

The mission is a significant step towards achieving self-reliance in edible oils. 

It reflects the government's commitment to supporting farmers and enhancing agriculture. 

The National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm is a transformative initiative. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable oil palm industry in India. 

The mission is expected to pave the way for a greener and more self-sufficient future. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this initiative. 

The government is committed to providing all necessary support for successful implementation. 

This mission is a crucial component of India's agricultural policy. 

It aims to ensure food security and improve the economic status of farmers. 

The National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm is a landmark initiative in Indian agriculture. 

It has the potential to change the landscape of edible oil production in the country. 

The mission will contribute to reducing the import bill and enhancing domestic production. 

Farmers are urged to participate actively in this mission for their benefit. 

The government is optimistic about achieving the targets set under this mission. 

The National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm is a significant development in India's agricultural journey.
